A 2-week SQL interview prep plan, day by day

Fourteen days. Days 1 to 9 take one SQL skill each, three questions a day from Easy up to Hard, in the order SQL Quest's learning path teaches them. Days 10 to 14 are the traps, your two weakest skills, a timed mock and its review. Before day 1, a ten-question readiness test shows which skill needs the spare time.

Every question below links to its page, with the prompt and the tables; solve it in the browser from there. The plan names 27 questions. What is free: 10 free challenge solves, plus the lessons, warm-ups and the daily challenge — Pro opens all 300+. A Hard marked Pro needs Pro; a Hard marked preview can be one of your free solves.

Day 0The readiness test

Ten questions, no signup. You get a Skillmap across the nine skills and the one to fix first. Note your weakest two: on any day whose skill you already pass, solve only the Hard question and give the rest of the hour to them.

Take the readiness test.

Day 1Querying Basics

SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY and LIMIT, until reading a table and filtering it takes no thought. Every other day builds on this one.

  1. Your First QueryEasy
  2. Pick Your ColumnsEasy
  3. Filter with WHEREEasy

The bank has no Medium or Hard question on this skill alone; the harder days build on it.

More on this skill: Querying Basics practice.

Day 2Aggregation & Grouping

COUNT, SUM and AVG per group, and HAVING to filter the groups. Say the grain of the result (one row per what?) before you write it.

  1. Counting RowsEasy
  2. GROUP BY + HAVINGMedium
  3. Customer Lifetime ValueHardPro

More on this skill: Aggregation & Grouping practice.

Day 3Joins

INNER and LEFT JOIN, and what happens to the rows that have no match. Count the rows before and after each join.

  1. Your First JOINEasy
  2. LEFT JOIN: Keep EveryoneMedium
  3. Customer Lifetime Value PipelineHardPro

More on this skill: Joins practice.

Day 4Conditional Logic

CASE WHEN to label, bucket and pivot rows. The first branch that matches wins, and a CASE with no ELSE returns NULL.

  1. Calculated ColumnsEasy
  2. Introduction to CASE WHENMedium
  3. Island Length ClassificationHardPro

More on this skill: Conditional Logic practice.

Day 5NULL Handling

IS NULL, COALESCE, and what NULL does to a comparison, a count and an average.

  1. Handling NULL ValuesEasy
  2. Handle NULL AgesMedium
  3. Blank Is Not NULL: A Port Data-Quality ReportHardPro

More on this skill: NULL Handling practice.

Day 6String Functions

Cleaning and matching text: TRIM, LOWER, SUBSTR, LIKE, and joining text with ||.

  1. Long-Named PassengersEasy
  2. Title Social Survival AnalysisMedium
  3. Passenger Family Survival AnalysisHardPro

More on this skill: String Functions practice.

Day 7Date Functions

Truncating to a month, the days between two dates, and ranges that include their last day.

  1. Monthly Order CountEasy
  2. Date Functions: How Long Ago?Medium
  3. Order Sessionization by CustomerHardPro

More on this skill: Date Functions practice.

Day 8Subqueries & CTEs

A value from a subquery, a filter from one, and a long query broken into named CTE steps.

  1. A Subquery That Returns One ValueEasy
  2. Simple Subquery: Above AverageMedium
  3. Correlated Subquery: Employees Above Department MedianHardPro

More on this skill: Subqueries & CTEs practice.

Day 9Window Functions

ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals and LAG: a value per row computed over a group, without collapsing the rows.

  1. Your First Window FunctionEasy
  2. Window Functions: ROW_NUMBERMedium
  3. Salary Rank Within DepartmentHardpreview

More on this skill: Window Functions practice.

Day 10The five SQL traps

Read the five trap pages. Each one is a query that runs, returns a plausible number and is wrong, with the fix beside it. Run each wrong query in your head before you read why.

  1. NOT IN with NULL
  2. Join fan-out
  3. BETWEEN on timestamps
  4. Average of averages
  5. LEFT JOIN with a WHERE filter

Day 11Your two weakest skills

Open the Coach. Its Skillmap now has nine days of your solves behind it; spend the day on the two lowest skills, on the questions the Coach picks next.

Open the Coach in the app; the Coach and its Skillmap are free.

Day 12A timed mock interview

Sit one mock as if it were the screen: one clock, no other tabs, no hints. The SQL Fundamentals Assessment is free; a Pro mock matches a role or a company.

What the timed mocks are, and which is free.

Day 13Review the mock

Read the one-sentence diagnosis under each wrong answer, then retry only the questions you missed. Re-solve any plan question you could not finish.

Day 14Retake the readiness test, then rest

Take the ten questions again and compare the Skillmap with day 0. Stop there: the day before the interview is for sleep, not a new topic.

Retake the readiness test.

Questions

Is two weeks enough to prepare for a SQL interview?

Two weeks is enough to work through the nine skills an interview draws on once each, practise the traps and sit a timed mock. It is not enough to learn SQL from zero; if day 1 feels new, start with the lessons in the app and stretch the plan.

How long does each day take?

A skill day is three questions, Easy, Medium and Hard. Give each question up to twenty minutes before you open a hint, so a day fits in an evening.

What if I already know some of these skills?

Take the readiness test on day 0. It scores you per skill; on a day whose skill you already pass, solve only the Hard question and spend the rest of the hour on your weakest skill.

Which parts of the plan are free?

The readiness test, the trap pages and the question pages are free to read. In the app: 10 free challenge solves, plus the lessons, warm-ups and the daily challenge — Pro opens all 300+. The Coach, the Skillmap and the SQL Fundamentals mock are free too; the other mocks are Pro.

Which SQL dialect does the plan use?

The questions run on SQLite in your browser. Joins, GROUP BY, CTEs and window functions are written the same way in PostgreSQL, MySQL and Snowflake, and each challenge in the app lists the functions that differ, dates first.
